messages.content: What were the stock prices of Apple Inc. listed on NASDAQ and Microsoft Corporation listed on NYSE for the past 10 and 15 days respectively?

function.name: get_stock_price
function.description: Retrieve the stock price for a specific company and time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company.description: The ticker symbol of the company.

days.description: Number of past days for which the stock price is required.

exchange.description: The stock exchange where the company is listed, default is NYSE

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What were the stock prices of Apple Inc. listed on NASDAQ and Microsoft Corporation listed on NYSE for the past 10 and 15 days respectively?" They want stock prices for Apple (NASDAQ) for past 10 days, and Microsoft (NYSE) for past 15 days.

We have a function get_stock_price that can retrieve stock price for a specific company and time frame. It takes company ticker symbol, days, exchange optional. We need to call this function twice: once for Apple with days=10, exchange="NASDAQ". And once for Microsoft with days=15, exchange="NYSE".

But note: Apple is actually listed on NASDAQ, ticker AAPL. Microsoft is listed on NASDAQ too, but the user says NYSE. Actually Microsoft is on NASDAQ too. But we will follow user request: exchange="NYSE" for Microsoft. Might not exist but we can still call.

We need to produce a function call. According to policy, we should call the function. The function returns any. We need to output the function call. Then the system will handle it. So we produce a JSON with function name and arguments.

We should not provide any other text. Just the function call.
